I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the safest path for me is the usual winter wheat plus summer maize system on the same land. I know this pattern, the buyers know it, and the water and machinery arrangement are easier for me to handle than trying something fancy. I would not spread myself across too many crops, because with my situation I would rather protect yield and reduce mistakes than chase a higher but uncertain return.

So I will use one year of double cropping on the same fields. I will put my land into winter wheat first, then follow it with summer maize. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put more fertilizer into nitrogen, irrigate several times because spring can turn dry, and keep disease and aphid control to a few timely sprays instead of many small ones. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into maize with hybrid seed, keep the stand even, use no-tillage seeding into the stubble to save time and moisture, and give fertilizer in a practical amount that matches local yield. I will not overdo pesticide use; I will spray when pressure is real. My goal is stable grain, manageable work, and lower risk.
